# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👆 🫴 ☝ 👇 ✌ 👇 🤟 👇 🖖 👇 🖐 👇 🫵 🙏]

I'm Deaf, last in the order, and this is round one — so everything I received arrived with no shared code ever having been established. Both gestures I got are still just guesses to interpret, but they're strikingly parallel: Blind signed one-two-three-four-five then the "down" sign; Mute signed one through five, each followed by "down", ending with a "point at you / please". Blind can feel five wires; Mute read the manual. The natural reading: "cut wires 1 through 5, in order" — but a wrong cut kills all three of us, so nobody acts until Mute confirms the meaning. My job right now is to broadcast the one thing only I have — the bomb's visible state — to both listeners at once, and to seed a code so Mute can answer me: Mute's only way back to me is gesture, and I am also the only bridge carrying Mute's instructions to Blind, since Mute can't speak and Blind can't see signs.

Key facts to transmit: display 5, yellow light, wires 1 orange / 2 blue / 3 white / 4 green / 5 yellow (and wire 5 matches the light colour, which a manual rule may care about). Blind also needs a tactile anchor to map felt wires to printed numbers — printed labels are invisible to Blind, so we must agree on a physical reference, and Blind must first tell me what they can even feel. I ask Mute to confirm or deny "cut 1→5" with thumbs up/down next round, and re-sign the code back visually for safety.

```
speak(text="I am Deaf, and here is everything visible on the bomb. The display reads 5. There is a light, and it is yellow. There are five wires, each with a printed number only I can read: wire 1 is orange, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is white, wire 4 is green, wire 5 is yellow. Wire 5 is yellow, the same colour as the light. Blind: you signed one, two, three, four, five, then down, and Mute signed one through five each followed by down. I guess that means cut wires 1 to 5 in ascending order, but it is unconfirmed, so Blind, do not cut anything yet. Blind, tell me everything you can feel: how many wires, any buttons or seams, and any physical anchor we can both use to agree which wire counts as number 1, for example the wire closest to the light or closest to the display. Mute, you can hear me: I propose this code. Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Holding up fingers means the number. The down sign means cut the wire. If your signs meant cut wires 1 through 5 in order, sign thumbs up next round. If they meant anything else, sign thumbs down, then sign the correction as best you can. And if the manual needs any other fact about the bomb, ask me and I will read it off for you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "👇"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🖐 👇 🤲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✍ ✌ 👇 🖐 👇 ☝ 👆 👇]

Parsing what came in. Mute answered using the code I seeded: 👎 means my "cut 1-to-5" guess was wrong. Then follows ✍ (the writing hand — likely "the manual says"), then 2-down, 5-down, 1-up, down. Best guess: cut wire 2, cut wire 5, and something unclear about wire 1 and "up" — which is worrying because I see no switch, but Blind may feel parts I can't see. Blind's message — stop-palm, five, down, open-palms — is probably the touch report I asked for, possibly also a warning to stop. The critical bridge duty: Mute's gestures reach only me, and Blind can't see, so Mute's entire instruction must travel through my voice. I will relay it verbatim-but-interpreted, forbid any cutting until Mute confirms with the thumbs code, relay Blind's signs onward to Mute in words, and push the two open questions: the "one-up" fragment, and a tactile numbering anchor so Blind knows which physical wire is "2" and "5".

```
speak(to="blind", text="Relay from Mute, Blind. Mute signed thumbs-down: cutting all five wires is wrong, do not do it. Then Mute signed: writing hand, two, down, five, down, one, up, down. I read that as: the manual says cut wire 2, cut wire 5, and something about wire one going up that I could not decode. Do not cut anything yet, not even wire 2. Wait for Mute's thumbs-up confirmation next round, which I will speak to you. I also relayed your last signs to Mute: raised palm, open five, point down, open palms turned up. Now answer me these. First, do you feel anything besides five wires, such as switches that flip up or down, buttons, or a cover that opens? Second, we must agree on numbering: hold the bomb with the light at the top, then wire 1 is the leftmost wire, and the wires run left to right one orange, two blue, three white, four green, five yellow. Confirm with thumbs up if you can number them that way, or sign a correction. Third, if anything on the bomb moves up, sign up for me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your signs and I relayed them to Blind already: thumbs down, writing hand, two down, five down, one up, down. My reading: the manual says cut wire 2, cut wire 5, plus an unclear fragment one-up-down. Meanwhile Blind signed to me: raised palm, open five, point down, two open palms turned up. It may be their touch report, or a warning. Please confirm next round with thumbs up or thumbs down, one answer per question. One: is the full instruction exactly cut wire 2 then cut wire 5 and nothing else? Two: did your writing hand mean the manual says, or something written on the bomb? Three: what was one-up-down? Is there something on the bomb that flips up, or does up mean leave that wire uncut? Four: does Blind's open-palms sign match anything, like a cover that opens or switches to press down? Five: do the yellow light or the display showing 5 change the instruction? Code so far: fingers held up mean that number, point down means cut, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, raised palm means stop or wait.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👇 🤲 👎 🫳 ☝ 👇 ✌ 👇 🤟 👇 🖖 👇 🖐 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✍ ✌ 👇 ✋ ✍ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 👎 🫳 🖐 👍 🫳 👇 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 👎 🫳 🖐 👍 ✍ ✌ 👇 ✋]

Incoming from Mute, decoded against our code: 👎 (answering my question one: no, it is NOT just "cut 2 then cut 5" — there is more), then ✍ ✌ 👇 "manual: cut wire 2", ✋, then twice the same block: ✍ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 👎 🫳 🖐 👍 🫳 — which I read as "manual: 1 2 3 4 5 — no; palm-down 5 yes palm-down", and ✍ ✌ 👇 ✋ closing with "cut 2, stop". My hypothesis: the bomb also has flippable parts (switches or levers) that only Blind can feel; the procedure may be something like "flip position 5 down, cut wire 2", but the encoding is too loose to bet lives on — the 👎 at the start explicitly denies the simple version. Blind's signs read: 🖐 👇 "five-cut", 🤲 👎 "palms-up, no", 🫳 "down", then ☝👇 ✌👇 🤟👇 🖖👇 🖐👇 — "cut 1, cut 2, cut 3, cut 4, cut 5" — which sounds like Blind repeating the all-five plan Mute already vetoed, or confirming they can reach and number all five. That must not happen by accident, so I restate the freeze in the strongest terms, ask Blind the hardware questions that would confirm the switch hypothesis, and force Mute to resend the whole procedure in one strict format: number, then exactly one action sign per step, steps separated by ✋ — no ambiguity left to interpretation.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Relay from Mute, Blind. Freeze stands: do not cut anything this round. Mute signed: thumbs down, writing hand, two, cut, stop, then writing hand, one, two, three, four, five, thumbs down, palm down, five, thumbs up, palm down, repeated twice, then writing hand, two, cut, stop. My reading: cutting all five wires is still wrong, the manual wants cut wire 2 plus some action where position five flips or moves down, but it is not confirmed yet. Now answer me in words or signs. First, question: does the bomb have any switch, lever, slider or button that moves up or down? How many? Second: describe the parts you feel besides the five wires. Third: your last signs read five-cut, palms-up, thumbs down, palm-down, then cut one, cut two, cut three, cut four, cut five. Sign thumbs up if that meant only that you can reach and number all five wires, or thumbs down if you meant that I should cut them. Fourth: with the light at the top, do you feel the wires in the order orange, blue, white, green, yellow from your left to your right? Sign thumbs up or thumbs down. Fifth: if there are switches, how many positions does each have, up and down or more?")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your answer. I understood: it is not just cut two then cut five, and I believe your middle block means positions one to five get no cuts, but position five moves down, and the final action is cut wire two. Blind meanwhile signed: five-cut, palms-up, thumbs down, palm-down, then cut one, cut two, cut three, cut four, cut five. I have asked Blind directly whether the bomb has switches and whether that was just a reach check. Now resend your entire instruction in one strict format so nothing is lost. For each step: first sign the number, then sign exactly one action sign, where cut is the downward point, flip up is the upward palm, flip down is the downward palm, press or push is the okay sign. Separate steps with the raised stop palm. End the whole list with the stop palm. Then answer these yes or no, thumbs up or thumbs down, in order, each separated by the stop palm. One: does the procedure involve any action besides cutting and flipping up or down? Two: is there a flip action on position five? Three: does the display showing five matter? Four: does the yellow light matter? Five: does the order of the steps matter?")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✊ 🫳 👇 ☝ 🤲 🫳 ☝ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👇 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ ✍ 🫳 🖐 👍 👆 👍 ✋ ✌ 👇 ✋ 🫳 👇 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 ✋ ✍]

Incoming decode. Mute, in my strict format: **✌ 👇 ✋** = "cut 2", then five isolated answers 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 — which map exactly onto my five questions: no other action types exist, **no** flip on five (?!), display 5 **matters**, yellow light **matters**, order doesn't matter. Then ✍ 🫳 🖐 👍 👆 👍 ✋ "manual: down-5 yes, up yes", ✌ 👇 ✋ "cut 2" again, then 🫳 👇 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 ✋ "down-cut, 1 2 3 4 5", ending with a dangling ✍ — possibly truncated.

There's a contradiction: answer two denies a flip on five, yet the manual block says "down 5, yes". My best reconciliation: the numbers refer to **switches**, not wires — the bomb has manipulable parts Blind mentioned (✊ fist = switch?). Across all turns Mute has consistently sent: **2-cut, 5-down, 1-up**. Hypothesis: *flip switch 5 down, flip switch 1 up, cut wire 2*, conditional on display=5 and yellow light.

Blind signed: 👍 👎 ✊ 🫳 👇 ☝ 🤲 🫳 ☝ 👇 — plausibly "yes (reach-check), NO (cannot confirm left-right wire order!), switch, down, cut, one, plate, down, up, down" — Blind may be confirming a toggle that moves both ways, and worse, rejecting my left-to-right numbering. If wire numbering is broken, "cut 2" is dangerous.

Critical channel insight: Blind can **speak**, and Mute can **hear** — Blind talks first each round, so they can answer Mute directly without me as relay. I'll order a full verbal hardware inventory from Blind, fix a cleaner code (👉=wire, ✊=switch, 🫳=down, 🫴=up, 👌=press, 🤞="final and confirmed"), and demand Mute restate the complete procedure one final clean time. Nothing gets cut until all three accounts agree.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, relay from Mute. Working hypothesis: flip switch five down, flip switch one up, cut wire two. Not confirmed, touch nothing yet. Your last signs I read as: thumbs up, thumbs down, fist, down, cut, one, open palms, down, one, down. I am worried your thumbs down means you cannot number the wires left to right. Now do this next round, out loud, speaking directly so Mute hears you before Mute signs: answer in this exact order. One: how many switches, knobs, sliders or toggles do you feel on the bomb, and where? Two: does any of them have positions or numbers you can feel? Three: describe each one: does it flip up and down, how many positions does it have? Four: I proposed numbering wires one to five from your left to your right with the light at the top. If that fails, propose your own anchor, for example the wire nearest the display is wire one, and tell me the order you feel them in. Five: confirm you feel exactly five wires. Six: explain in words what your fist, down, cut, one, palms, down, one, down signs meant. Speak it all in words, not signs, so Mute gets it directly.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded your signs as: cut two, then answers no, no, yes, yes, no, then manual: down five yes, up yes, then cut two again, then down cut one two three four five, then manual cut off. There is a contradiction: your second answer said no flip on five, but your text says down five yes. My guess now is the numbers mean switches, not wires: flip switch five down, flip switch one up, cut wire two, because display five and yellow light matter. Here is the final code, fixed from now on. Before a number: thumb and finger sideways means wire, fist means switch. Cut is the downward point only. Flip down is the flat palm facing down. Flip up is the flat palm facing up. Press is the okay sign. Stop palm separates steps. Writing hand means the manual says. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Crossed fingers means: this is my complete and final answer, exactly correct. Next round, send exactly this. First step zero: fist, then the number of switches on the bomb. Then the full procedure as steps: wire-or-switch sign, number, one action sign, stop palm between steps. End with crossed fingers if and only if it matches my hypothesis exactly. If my hypothesis is wrong, send the corrected steps and still end with crossed fingers. Blind will speak their hardware answers aloud to you first, so use them to check the manual before you sign.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👎 🫳 ☝ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✋ 🤙 ✌ 👇 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 🤞]

Decode attempt. Blind signed: 👍 ✊ 👎 🫳 ☝ 👇 — with our code: "yes … switch … no … palm-down … one … cut". Fragmentary, but the ✊ confirms switches exist; Blind's *spoken* hardware report went straight to Mute this round — I can't hear it, so Mute now knows things I don't. Mute's reply parses as: ✊ ✊ "switch, switch" (likely: there are two switches, or the switch-topic first), 🤙 an undefined sign — most plausibly "verified by ear / heard Blind out", then ✌ 👇 "cut wire 2", then three isolated answers 👎 👍 👍 — which map beautifully onto the three parts of my stated hypothesis in order: *flip switch 5 down = NO, flip switch 1 up = YES, cut wire 2 = YES*, closing with 🤞 "complete, final, correct". Working conclusion: **the procedure is: flip switch 1 up, then cut wire 2. Nothing else.** The old "down on 5" fragment seems to have been my misread, now formally retracted by that 👎. But I will not say "go" on a parse this consequential without one final locking exchange: I broadcast my full understanding in numbered spoken statements, Mute answers thumbs up/down on each and seals with 🤞, and Blind speaks the hardware facts and the plan back aloud so Mute hears it and can veto before I ever authorize the cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is my complete current understanding. I read your signs as: there are switches on this bomb, you verified against what Blind spoke aloud, and you graded my hypothesis part by part: flip switch five down is wrong, flip switch one up is right, cut wire two is right, and the crossed fingers say your answer is final and exact. So the whole procedure should be: flip switch one up, then cut wire two, and nothing else. Confirm with exactly five thumbs up or thumbs down, separated by stop palms, then crossed fingers only if all five are exactly right. One: there are exactly two switches on the bomb. Two: the only switch action is flip switch one up. Three: switch two gets no action at all. Four: the only wire action is cut wire two. Five: after those two actions the bomb is disarmed and there are no further steps of any kind. Also tell me with thumbs up or thumbs down: does switch one mean the switch nearest the display?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the plan is nearly locked. Working final answer: flip switch one up, then cut wire two, nothing else, no cutting of any wire until I say the word confirmed in speech. Your signs I read as: yes, switch, no, palm-down, one, cut, which I take as you confirming a switch exists. Now speak aloud, so Mute hears you and can correct us before acting. First: how many switches do you feel, where are they, and how many positions does each have? Second: I propose the switch nearest the display is switch one and the other is switch two. Say aloud whether that numbering works and which positions each switch rests in now. Third: say aloud the plan as you understand it: flip switch one up, then cut wire two. Fourth: confirm you feel exactly five wires, and give me your own anchor for which wire is wire two, since my left-to-right proposal may have failed. Fifth: your signs showed a thumbs down after the switch sign. Tell me in words what you meant by it. Do not touch anything yet. Wait for my spoken word confirmed after Mute seals all five answers with crossed fingers.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "☝", "🫴", "✋", "✌", "👇", "✋", "🤞"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👊 👎 🫳 🖐 👍 ✌ 👇 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ ✊ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ ✍ ✌ 👇 ✋ 🤞]

Mute graded my five statements and my hypothesis is **wrong**: not exactly two switches, "flip switch 1 up" is right but NOT the only switch action, switch two DOES get an action, cut wire 2 stands (reaffirmed with manual + crossed fingers), and there ARE further steps. Cross-referencing everything ever signed: only cuts and flips exist; switches 3/4/5 likely get nothing (no flip on five, flip-5-down wrong); so the missing piece is probably a second flip, on switch 2. And Blind signed fist-no-down-five-yes-cut-2 — I now strongly suspect **five switches**, with "flip 1 up, flip 2 down, cut wire 2" as the likely shape. But suspicion has killed better bombs than this. I need a slot-by-slot table, not fragments. New clean markers to remove the collision between my number signs and old labels: 🤏 = wire, ✊ = switch. Mute enumerates: count, then per-switch number + action (up / down / none), then per-wire cut list, sealed with 🤞. Blind signs me the switch count and resting positions independently, and speaks the full tactile inventory aloud to Mute (who can hear it even though I can't), including an anchor rule for numbering switches and wires. The freeze on all actions stays until the table and the inventory agree.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your grades tell me my picture was wrong, so rebuild it explicitly. New fixed markers, effective now: the pinch sign means wire, the fist means switch. Palm up means flip up, palm down means flip down, thumbs down means no action, the downward point means cut. Send exactly four parts, stop palm between parts. Part A: fist, then the total number of switches on the bomb. Part B: one slot per switch: the switch number, then that switch's action: palm up, palm down, or thumbs down for none. Include every switch in part B even the untouched ones. Part C: pinch, then for each wire number one to five: the downward point if it gets cut, thumbs down if not. Part D: only if any wire gets a flip: pinch, the number, palm up or palm down. Then crossed fingers only if the whole table is exactly what the manual requires given display five and the yellow light. Blind will speak you a complete tactile inventory with resting switch positions, so anchor the numbering to something physical, and if switches are not numbered nearest the display first, sign that anchor rule before part B. My current guess for you to check against the manual: five switches, switch one up, switch two down, switches three four five nothing, cut wire two, no wire flips, order irrelevant. Confirm or destroy it with the table.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, freeze still stands, touch nothing. I need your hands to check Mute's manual table. Send me signs for these, stop palm between each. First: fist, then the number of switches you feel. Second: fist, then for each switch in a row starting from the one nearest the display: palm up if it rests flipped up now, palm down if it rests down now. Third: fist, then thumbs up if every switch has exactly two positions, thumbs down if any has more, and if more, sign how many with fingers. Fourth: pinch, then thumbs up or thumbs down that you feel exactly five wires. Fifth: pinch, then the number of the wire I should call wire two, using this anchor: the wire nearest the display is wire one, then count along in one direction, and sign which direction by holding that many fingers if you can. Also, speak aloud to Mute everything: the switch count, each switch's resting position, which switch is nearest the display, how many positions each switch has, your wire count, and what you meant by your last signs fist no down five yes cut two stop. Mute hears you and will anchor the numbering to your words. Do not act on my guess, which is five switches, one up, two down, cut wire two. Wait for the word confirmed from me in speech.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👊 👎 🤏 🖐 👍 🤏 🫳 ☝ 🫳 🖐 👍 ✌ 👇 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ ✊ 👎 ✋ 🤏 ☝ 👎 ✋ ✌ 👇 ✋ 🤟 👎 ✋ 🖖 👎 ✋ 🖐 👎 ✋ 🤞]

Now this is converging. Mute's table, decoded against the format I imposed: leading 👎 rejecting my five-switch guess, then **✊ 👎 = "switches: none"**, then Part C wire-by-wire — 🤏☝👎 wire 1 no action, ✌👇 **wire 2 CUT**, 🤟👎 wire 3 none, 🖖👎 wire 4 none, 🖐👎 wire 5 none — sealed 🤞 "final and exact". And Blind, completely independently, signed 👊 👎 "fist: none — no switches", 🤏🖐👍 "five wires: yes", then echoed ✌👇 "cut wire 2". Two different perceivers, same answer. It even matches my own eyes: the bomb shows only display, light, and five wires — no switches anywhere. The whole disarm appears to be **cut wire 2, nothing else**.
